Coastal Reclaim Atlas

How the numbers are made

Plants: HydroWASTE v1.0 (Ehalt Macedo et al. 2022) entries that are operational or of unreported status, with the estimated outfall within 50 km of the ocean (HydroWASTE COAST_50KM flag confirmed against the Natural Earth coastline, so large-lake plants are excluded). Ocean outfalls are plants for which HydroWASTE estimates the outfall to be the ocean or an estuary (no river reach), after corrections from checks of the 25 largest plants against utility sources (Indonesian synthetic plants removed); river outfalls discharge to rivers near the coast and are shown for reference only. Potable product is 90% of the treated flow diverted (80 to 95%) times 80% overall recovery (70 to 85%).

Energy: potable reuse (MF/UF, RO, UV-AOP) at 1.0 kWh/m³ of product (0.8 to 1.5), plus 0.3 kWh/m³ of feed for plants with primary treatment only; seawater RO at 3.5 kWh/m³ (3.0 to 4.0); both exclude conveyance. PV is sized from NASA POWER long-term irradiance at the outfall with a 0.80 performance ratio, 5 m² per kWp and a 0.40 ground-coverage ratio. Brine avoided is seawater RO brine at 42% recovery minus the concentrate of potable reuse. CO₂ uses the country's latest grid intensity (Ember via Our World in Data). Headline tiles are Monte Carlo medians for ocean outfalls; plant values use central parameters.

Water stress: WRI Aqueduct 4.0 baseline water stress of the sub-basin at the outfall. Data tier: A, treated flow reported; B, flow estimated from reported population equivalents; C, both population and flow modelled by HydroWASTE (treat with caution).

Priority score (0 to 100) is the mean of five equally weighted 0 to 1 terms: Aqueduct stress category, solar irradiance (2.5 to 6 kWh m⁻² d⁻¹), grid carbon intensity (0 to 900 g/kWh), the share of the country's population without safely managed drinking water (WHO/UNICEF JMP 2025), and plant size (log flow, 5th to 95th percentile). It is a screening aid, not a design value.
